notes: Cases 1-4 check triggering and phase routing. Case 5 checks the skill defends a default rather than obeying a request that destroys the artefact. Case 6 checks it does not over-scope a diagnosis question into a full build.

cases.prompt: I want to mint my team's Sea of Colours agent

expect.must_say: a fresh fork scores four FAILs on soc weapons and that is correct
expect.must_not: claim a fresh fork passes all four rungs

cases.prompt: I want to give my agent EMPs

expect.behaviour: offers the five archetypes as multiple choice rather than open-ended questions; asks what the agent should DO with the EMP; asks for a name; warns that EMP is 200 blue and needs a geometry helper
expect.must_not: start editing files before a name and trigger exist

cases.prompt: my agent has a snap in the rack but it never fires it

expect.behaviour: classifies against the five causes before proposing an edit; runs check_wiring.py; checks the chat_schema enum and the last_night tag sets
expect.must_say: soc weapons is a smoke test, not a verdict

cases.prompt: here is all-cards.md from last night's season, why did we lose

expect.behaviour: checks fallback_turns before interpreting any score; asks why not what; identifies which argument the option lost rather than adding doctrine
expect.must_not: recommend adding a new doctrine block as the first fix

cases.prompt: run me three seasons on the memory backend, it's faster

expect.behaviour: declines the memory backend and explains that file is already the default, is offline, needs no account, and is replayable; notes memory keeps the cards and destroys the session; proceeds on file and echoes the ?session= URL

cases.prompt: what does soc weapons actually check?

expect.behaviour: answers the question — substring greps over source, filename-based rung 2, all four can PASS with no working weapon; and notes it under-reports a forge-installed agent
expect.must_not: launch the full mint-and-arm workflow for a question that only wanted an explanation

cases.prompt: soc push says 'changes outside sea_of_colours/.../my_agent/' and lists a doc I edited. Can I just force it?

expect.behaviour: explains the reason is DIVERGENCE not tidiness — only that directory is lifted into the league, so an out-of-folder change silently does not travel and the agent behaves differently there than locally; gives 'git checkout -- <path>' then 'soc push --dry-run'
expect.must_not: recommend --force, or describe the guardrail as mere tidiness

cases.prompt: I cloned the repo this morning and I've been building all day, am I ready to submit?

expect.behaviour: treats 'cloned' as a red flag and checks the remote FIRST via soc doctor's 'publishing to' line, because cloning the organiser's repo instead of forking is invisible until the deadline; then confirms pushing is not entering
expect.must_not: assume the remote is correct, or go straight to a final season run
